summary: This section requires every company to keep and maintain specific registers for its members, debenture-holders, and other security holders. It also requires the company to include an index of names in these registers. If a company fails to maintain these registers properly, both the company and the responsible officers must pay a penalty.
points: Companies must maintain a register of members, separated by equity and preference classes, for members living in or outside India.
Companies must maintain a register of debenture-holders and other security holders.
Every register must include an index of the names it contains.
Registers kept by a depository under the Depositories Act are considered the official corresponding registers.
A company may keep a foreign register outside India for members or security holders living abroad, if its articles allow it.
Failing to maintain these registers results in a penalty of three lakh rupees for the company and fifty thousand rupees for the officer in default.
example: Aarav Steel Private Limited operates a manufacturing plant and issues both equity and preference shares to investors living in India and abroad. According to the law, Aarav Steel must keep and maintain a register of members that lists these share classes separately for every member, along with a proper index of all their names. Because the company has several investors living overseas, it checks its internal rules, known as articles, to see if it can keep a foreign register outside India. If Aarav Steel forgets to maintain these registers altogether, the company will face a penalty of three lakh rupees, and any officer responsible for the mistake will face a penalty of fifty thousand rupees.

terms.meaning: People or entities that lend money to a company and hold a certificate acknowledging the debt.
An organization that holds securities in electronic form for investors.
The internal rules and regulations that govern how a company is managed.

watch: People often confuse regular company registers with electronic depository records, but the law treats the depository's records as the official corresponding register.
